display.title: Episode 461: The Lost Letter, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: A mailbox letter about learning the Shema leads to the secret of the word Echad; then a wealthy student of the Baal Shem Tov turns down a brachah, and his fortune begins to slip away.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with a dive into his overloaded mailbox. The lucky letter, from a young listener in New Jersey, asks for a sheet with the words of the Shema to learn by heart. Uncle Yossi explains why the Shema is so important and what the word Echad means: aleph is one, for the One Hashem; ches is eight, for the seven heavens and the earth; and daled is four, for the four directions. Hashem is everywhere. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school recites the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time begins 'The Lost Letter'. On his last days, the Baal Shem Tov blesses his students, but the wealthy and generous Reb Leibel feels he has everything and asks for no brachah. The Baal Shem Tov gives him a sealed letter to deliver to Reb Shalom. On the way home the letter slips under a closet and is forgotten. One misfortune after another follows, and Reb Leibel wonders what he has done wrong. To be continued next week.
display.lesson: No matter how well things are going, we always need Hashem's blessing, so we daven every day and value the brachah of a tzaddik.
